main_text.p: cap. 8. Quòd acidum in frigido subtilis consistat, uti austerum in frigido crasso. Et sanè Galenus 1. c. lib. iv. cap. 24. acetum vocat refrigerans & repellens; uti postea ibid. lib. iv. cap. 24. Aci-dum, inquit, omne quod tantum est aci-dum, quicquid id fuerit, plane frigidum est, sive pyrum, sive malum, sive acinus uvæ, sive rubi, Mora, sive mala Punica, sive quivis alius fructus, sive succus sive planta, ut oxylapathum sive oxalis; quip-pe si gustanti vehementem atque manife-stam illi inesse aciditatem apparet, nec quicquam præ se ferat acrimonia, omni-nò hunc succum refrigerantem reperies, quin confidenter utitor, sive ad ardores, uti consultum est, hypochondriis impositò, sive ad Erysipelas, sive ad alium affectum calidum. Ab usu igitur Medico, à Ju-vantibus & Lædentibus probat Gale-nus mille locis acida esse frigida. Sed Galenum nihilominus suum vocat, pro sese citat levis armaturæ miles. Qui cùm hactenus sub Galeno delitescere

page.notes: Catchword "tescere" at the foot right is the continuation of "delitescere" and is kept as the last word of the text. Some italic passages are printed with the Galenic citations in roman; the marginal running head has no separate figure.
